revenue:
On January 1, 2026, TechScale LLC enters into a bundled contract with a enterprise client for a total contract price of $240,000. The contract includes:
1. An enterprise software license (delivered immediately, standalone selling price = $150,000).
2. 24 months of technical support (standalone selling price = $90,000).
3. Implementation services completed on March 31, 2026 (standalone selling price = $60,000).
Required:
• Calculate the transaction price allocation for each performance obligation based on relative standalone selling prices.
• Provide the journal entry on January 1, 2026, assuming the entire $240,000 was collected upfront.
• Compute the total revenue recognized for the calendar year ending December 31, 2026.
lease:
A company enters into a 5-year operating lease for office space beginning January 1, 2026. Annual lease payments are $50,000, due every December 31. The company’s incremental borrowing rate is 6%. The present value factor of an ordinary annuity for 5 periods at 6% is 4.21236.
Required:
• Compute the initial valuation of the Right-of-Use (ROU) Asset and Lease Liability on January 1, 2026.
• Calculate the total Lease Expense for Year 1 (2026).
• Calculate the carrying value of the Lease Liability on December 31, 2026, after the first payment is made.
combination:
ParentCorp acquires 100% of SubInc for cash consideration of $850,000. On the acquisition date, SubInc’s book value of net assets is $500,000. An independent appraisal determines the following fair value adjustments:
• Equipment is undervalued by $80,000.
• An unrecorded trade name is valued at $120,000.
• SubInc has a contingent liability from a pending lawsuit valued at $30,000.
Required:
• Calculate the total identifiable net assets acquired at fair value.
• Calculate the resulting Goodwill or Bargain Purchase Gain from this transaction.
• Draft the consolidated opening elimination journal entry.
dvlifo:
A retail company adopts the Dollar-Value LIFO method on January 1, 2025.
• Base Year (Jan 1, 2025) Inventory: $300,000 (Price Index = 1.00)
• Dec 31, 2025 Inventory at ending prices: $363,000 (Price Index = 1.10)
• Dec 31, 2026 Inventory at ending prices: $430,000 (Price Index = 1.25)
Required:
• Deflate the ending inventories for both 2025 and 2026 to base-year costs.
• Determine the layer added or eroded during 2025 and 2026.
• Calculate the final Dollar-Value LIFO ending inventory balance for December 31, 2026.
eps:
For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2026, NetCo reported Net Income of $1,200,000. NetCo had 500,000 shares of common stock outstanding throughout the year. The company also had:
• 10,000 shares of 5%, $100 par value convertible cumulative preferred stock outstanding (each preferred share is convertible into 4 shares of common stock).
• $1,000,000 of 6% convertible bonds outstanding issued at par, convertible into a total of 50,000 common shares. The corporate tax rate is 21%.
Required:
• Calculate Basic Earnings Per Share (EPS).
• Test the convertible preferred stock and convertible bonds for anti-dilution.
• Calculate the fully Diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) for 2026.
cashflow:
For 2026, Apex Corp reports Net Income of $450,000. A comparison of its 2025 and 2026 balance sheets shows the following:
• Accounts Receivable increased by $35,000
• Inventory decreased by $22,000
• Prepaid Insurance increased by $5,000
• Accounts Payable increased by $18,000
• Income Tax Payable decreased by $12,000
• Depreciation Expense for the year was $65,000
• The company realized a $15,000 gain on the sale of equipment.
Required:
• Reconcile Net Income to Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities using the indirect method. Show every single addition and subtraction step.
materiality:
During the annual audit of MagnaCorp, the audit team sets Financial Statement Materiality at $500,000 and Performance Materiality at $375,000 (75%). During testing, the team uncovers three uncorrected errors:
1. Overstatement of ending inventory by $180,000.
2. Understatement of accrued liabilities by $140,000.
3. Premature revenue recognition cutoff error overstating revenue by $210,000.
Required:
• Calculate the aggregate factual misstatement found by the audit team.
• Evaluate whether the aggregate misstatements exceed overall materiality and performance materiality.
• Formulate the required auditor communication strategy and explain the impact on the audit opinion if management refuses to post adjustments.
pps:
An auditor is using Probability-Proportional-to-Size (PPS) sampling to test an accounts receivable population with a total book value of $6,000,000.
• Tolerable misstatement = $300,000
• Reliability factor for zero overstatements at a 95% confidence level = 3.00
• Expansion factor = 1.6
Required:
• Calculate the required sampling interval.
• Calculate the required sample size.
• If a logical unit with a book value of $15,000 is sampled and found to have an audited value of $12,000, calculate the resulting tainting percentage and projected misstatement for this sample item.
npv:
Matrix Energy is considering a capital investment project requiring an initial cash outlay of $800,000. The project has a 4-year lifespan with no salvage value. Net cash inflows are projected as:
• Year 1: $300,000
• Year 2: $350,000
• Year 3: $280,000
• Year 4: $200,000
• The company’s Weighted Average Capital Cost (WACC) is 10%. Present value factors at 10% are: Y1 = 0.9091, Y2 = 0.8264, Y3 = 0.7513, Y4 = 0.6830.
Required:
• Calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) of the project.
• Compute the exact Payback Period.
• Determine whether the project should be accepted or rejected based on financial theory metrics.
dupont:
Vanguard Manufacturing provides the following financial indicators for the fiscal year ending 2026:
• Total Sales = $5,000,000
• Net Income = $400,000
• Total Assets (Beginning) = $2,800,000 ; Total Assets (Ending) = $3,200,000
• Total Equity (Beginning) = $1,400,000 ; Total Equity (Ending) = $1,600,000
Required:
• Calculate the Net Profit Margin.
• Calculate the Asset Turnover Ratio and Equity Multiplier using average balance sheet balances.
• Apply the 3-step DuPont Analysis to compute and verify the exact Return on Equity (ROE).
